clauses.rationale: CM-07 least functionality restricts available utilities. CM-11 controls user-installed software including utilities. AC-06 least privilege restricts access to privileged utilities.
clauses.gaps: ISO 27002 specifically addresses privileged utility programs that can override system and application controls. SP 800-53 addresses through general least functionality and privilege controls rather than utility-specific controls.

clauses.title: Installation of software on operational systems
clauses.rationale: CM-05 access restrictions for change controls who can install. CM-07 least functionality limits what can be installed. CM-11 controls user-installed software. SA-22 addresses unsupported components. CM-14 (Signed Components) prevents installation of unsigned software/firmware, ensuring only verified software is installed on operational systems.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. CM-14 adds digital signature verification for software installation, strengthening operational system integrity.

clauses.title: Networks security
clauses.rationale: SC-07 boundary protection; SC-08 transmission confidentiality and integrity; AC-04 information flow enforcement. CA-09 (Internal System Connections) addresses authorization, documentation, and review of internal system connections, strengthening network security controls for internal network management.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. CA-09 adds internal connection authorization and documentation, complementing perimeter-focused SC-07.

clauses.title: Security of network services
clauses.rationale: SC-07/SC-08 cover network security mechanisms. SA-09 covers external system services including network services with security requirements and monitoring.
clauses.gaps: Minor: ISO 27002 requires security features, service levels, and management requirements for network services including SLAs. Network service-specific level agreements are less detailed in SP 800-53.

clauses.title: Segregation of networks
clauses.rationale: SC-07 boundary protection includes network segmentation capabilities. SC-32 system partitioning provides logical and physical separation. Together they comprehensively address network segregation.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. SP 800-53 network segmentation controls are comprehensive.

clauses.title: Web filtering
clauses.rationale: SC-07 boundary protection includes content filtering. SI-03 malware protection catches web-borne threats. AC-04 information flow enforcement.
clauses.gaps: ISO 27002 specifically addresses URL filtering, web content filtering, and restricting access to unsafe websites. No dedicated SP 800-53 web filtering control exists; addressed through general boundary and content controls.

clauses.title: Use of cryptography
clauses.rationale: SC-12 cryptographic key establishment and management. SC-13 cryptographic protection with algorithm requirements. SC-28 protection of information at rest using encryption.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. SP 800-53 cryptography controls are comprehensive including key management lifecycle.

clauses.title: Secure development life cycle
clauses.rationale: SA-03 system development life cycle with security integration. SA-08 security and privacy engineering principles. SA-10 developer configuration management. SA-11 developer testing and evaluation. SA-15 development process, standards, and tools. SA-17 developer security and privacy architecture and design.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. SP 800-53 SA family is comprehensive for secure development lifecycle.

clauses.title: Application security requirements
clauses.rationale: SA-04 acquisition process includes security functional requirements. SA-08 security engineering principles applied to application design. SA-11 developer testing validates security requirements are met.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. SP 800-53 application security requirements are well covered through acquisition and engineering controls.

clauses.title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
clauses.rationale: SA-08 security and privacy engineering principles. SA-17 developer security architecture and design. SC-07/SC-32 provide architecture-level security controls. PL-08 security and privacy architectures.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. SP 800-53 architecture and engineering controls are comprehensive.

clauses.title: Secure coding
clauses.rationale: SA-11 developer security testing validates code security. SA-15 development process standards and tools includes coding standards. SA-16 developer-provided training includes secure coding practices.
clauses.gaps: Minor: ISO 27002 provides specific secure coding practice guidance including input validation, error handling, and code review. SP 800-53 addresses through development process and testing controls rather than explicit coding standard requirements.

clauses.title: Security testing in development and acceptance
clauses.rationale: SA-11 directly covers developer security testing and evaluation. CA-02 security assessments for acceptance testing. SA-04 includes testing requirements in acquisition.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. SP 800-53 security testing controls are comprehensive.

clauses.title: Outsourced development
clauses.rationale: SA-04 acquisition requirements for outsourced development. SA-09 external system services. SA-10/SA-11 developer requirements apply to outsourced developers. SA-21 (Developer Screening) adds screening requirements for developers of critical system components, ensuring outsourced developers meet security trustworthiness standards.
clauses.gaps: Minor: ISO 27002 details outsourced development supervision, intellectual property rights, and acceptance testing. SP 800-53 covers through general acquisition and developer controls; SA-21 strengthens developer trust assurance.

clauses.title: Separation of development, test and production environments
clauses.rationale: CM-04 impact analysis requires separate test environments. SA-11 developer testing implies testing environments. SC-32 system partitioning supports environment separation. CM-02 baseline configuration with variants for different environments.
clauses.gaps: Minor: ISO 27002 explicitly requires development, testing, and production environment separation. SP 800-53 implies but does not mandate specific three-way environment separation.

clauses.title: Change management
clauses.rationale: CM-03 configuration change control with documented approval processes. CM-04 impact analysis before changes. CM-05 access restrictions for change. SA-10 developer configuration management for development changes.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. SP 800-53 change management controls are comprehensive.

clauses.title: Test information
clauses.rationale: SA-11 covers testing requirements. SA-15 development process standards includes test data management practices.
clauses.gaps: ISO 27002 specifically addresses protection of test data including anonymization, controlled use of production data for testing, and proper disposal of test data. SP 800-53 lacks an explicit test data management control.

clauses.title: Protection of information systems during audit testing
clauses.rationale: CA-02 covers security assessments including audit considerations and planning. AU-06 audit review analysis. CA-08 penetration testing addresses planned security testing with controls to protect systems during testing activities.
clauses.gaps: ISO 27002 requires that audit testing be planned and agreed to minimize business disruption, that access to tools is controlled, and that requirements are agreed with management. SP 800-53 assessment controls do not explicitly address protection of systems during audit activities.

frameworks.name: COBIT 2019
frameworks.description: Framework for IT governance and management. Helps organizations develop, implement, and improve IT governance and management practices.

metadata.disclaimer: Based on publicly available crosswalks and expert analysis. Incorporates new SP 800-53 Rev 5 controls where they genuinely improve coverage. Validate with qualified assessors for compliance/audit use.

clauses.title: Ensured Governance Framework Setting and Maintenance
clauses.rationale: PM-01 program plan; PM-02 roles; PM-03 resources; PM-09 risk strategy; PL-09 (new in Rev 5) central management of security controls strengthens governance framework; PL-10 (new in Rev 5) baseline selection supports governance-level decisions on control standards. SP 800-53 addresses security governance but COBIT EDM01 covers IT governance broadly.
clauses.gaps: COBIT EDM01 encompasses enterprise IT governance framework, governance system design, and optimization. SP 800-53 is security-focused and doesn't address broader IT governance structure, value delivery, or stakeholder transparency. PL-09/PL-10 improve central governance capability but don't close the enterprise IT governance gap.

clauses.title: Ensured Benefits Delivery
clauses.rationale: PM-01 program objectives; PM-03 resources; PM-06 measures of performance.
clauses.gaps: Significant gap. SP 800-53 doesn't address IT benefits delivery, value optimization, or portfolio management. Security is one component of IT value; COBIT covers full business value lifecycle.

clauses.title: Ensured Risk Optimization
clauses.rationale: PM-09 risk management strategy; RA-01 risk assessment policy; RA-03 risk assessment; PM-28 risk framing; RA-07 (new in Rev 5) risk response adds explicit risk treatment actions; RA-09 (new in Rev 5) criticality analysis identifies critical components for risk prioritization. Together these strengthen the risk optimization lifecycle.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 comprehensively addresses security risk. COBIT EDM03 covers enterprise-wide IT risk optimization including risk appetite, risk tolerance levels, and business-aligned risk management beyond security. RA-07/RA-09 improve response and criticality but enterprise risk aggregation across all IT remains a gap.

clauses.title: Ensured Resource Optimization
clauses.rationale: PM-03 security resources; PM-13 workforce; SA-03 lifecycle resources.
clauses.gaps: Significant gap. COBIT EDM04 covers all IT resource optimization (people, technology, data). SP 800-53 addresses security resources only, not enterprise IT resource planning and optimization.

clauses.title: Ensured Stakeholder Engagement
clauses.rationale: PM-01 program plan communicates to stakeholders; PM-02 assigns stakeholder roles.
clauses.gaps: Major gap. COBIT EDM05 covers stakeholder communication, transparency, and engagement across all IT activities. SP 800-53 doesn't address stakeholder engagement methodology or IT reporting to business.

clauses.title: Managed I&T Management Framework
clauses.rationale: PM-01/PL-01 establish security management framework; PM-02 roles; PM-03 resources; PL-09 (new in Rev 5) central management provides a mechanism for unified control administration that supports I&T framework operations.
clauses.gaps: COBIT APO01 covers full I&T management framework including organizational design, process management, and continuous improvement. SP 800-53 addresses security management only. PL-09 improves central management but doesn't address IT organizational design.

clauses.title: Managed Strategy
clauses.rationale: PM-01 security program; PM-07 enterprise architecture; PM-08 critical infrastructure; PM-11 mission processes.
clauses.gaps: Major gap. COBIT APO02 covers enterprise IT strategy, digital transformation, and strategic alignment. SP 800-53 addresses security strategy as a component but not IT strategic planning.

clauses.title: Managed Enterprise Architecture
clauses.rationale: PM-07 enterprise architecture; PL-08 security architecture; SA-08/SA-17 security engineering and design.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 covers security architecture well. COBIT APO03 covers full enterprise architecture (business, data, application, technology layers). Security architecture is one view.

clauses.title: Managed Innovation
clauses.rationale: PM-01 may include innovation aspects; SA-08 security engineering principles.
clauses.gaps: Major gap. SP 800-53 doesn't address IT innovation management, emerging technology assessment, or innovation enablement.

clauses.title: Managed Portfolio
clauses.rationale: PM-07 enterprise architecture includes portfolio awareness; PM-11 mission/business process definition.
clauses.gaps: Major gap. COBIT APO05 covers IT portfolio management, investment decisions, and program/project prioritization. Not in SP 800-53 scope.

clauses.title: Managed Budget and Costs
clauses.rationale: PM-03 addresses security resource allocation.
clauses.gaps: Major gap. COBIT APO06 covers full IT budgeting, cost management, and financial planning. SP 800-53 only addresses security resource allocation.

clauses.title: Managed Human Resources
clauses.rationale: PM-13 security workforce; PS family personnel security including PS-09 (new in Rev 5) position descriptions which defines security responsibilities in role descriptions; AT family training including AT-06 (new in Rev 5) training feedback for measuring training effectiveness. These additions strengthen HR coverage by linking security to job roles and measuring training outcomes.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 covers security-related HR (screening, training, roles). PS-09 and AT-06 improve role definition and training measurement. COBIT APO07 covers full IT HR management including skills planning, career development, and resource acquisition for all IT roles — not just security roles.

clauses.title: Managed Relationships
clauses.rationale: PM-15 security groups/contacts; SA-09 external system services.
clauses.gaps: Major gap. COBIT APO08 covers business-IT relationship management, service catalogs, and customer satisfaction. SP 800-53 only covers security-specific relationships.

clauses.title: Managed Service Level Agreements
clauses.rationale: SA-04 acquisition requirements; SA-09 external service agreements; CA-03 information exchange agreements.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 covers security aspects of service agreements. COBIT APO09 covers full SLA management including service catalog, service level definition, and performance monitoring.

clauses.title: Managed Vendors
clauses.rationale: SA-04/SA-09 acquisition and service requirements; SR family supply chain. Security vendor management well covered.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 comprehensively covers security aspects of vendor management. COBIT APO10 also covers commercial management, contract negotiation, and vendor performance optimization beyond security.

clauses.title: Managed Quality
clauses.rationale: SA-11 developer testing; SA-15 development standards; CM-04 impact analysis; CA-02 assessments.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 covers security testing quality. COBIT APO11 covers enterprise quality management system, QA standards, and continuous improvement for all IT services.

clauses.title: Managed Risk
clauses.rationale: RA family comprehensive risk assessment; RA-07 (new in Rev 5) risk response provides explicit risk treatment; RA-08 (new in Rev 5) privacy impact assessments extend risk to privacy domain; RA-09 (new in Rev 5) criticality analysis strengthens risk-based prioritization; PM-09/PM-28 risk strategy/framing; CA-05 remediation. Security and privacy risk management now very strong.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 is strong on security/privacy risk. COBIT APO12 extends to IT operational risk, project risk, and enterprise risk integration. RA-07/RA-08/RA-09 close significant gaps from v1.0 but SP 800-53 remains focused on information security/privacy risk.

clauses.title: Managed Security
clauses.rationale: PM-01 program plan; PM-02 roles; PM-03 resources; PM-06 performance; PM-09 risk strategy; PL-01/PL-02 planning; PL-09 (new in Rev 5) central management enables unified ISMS-style control governance; PL-10 (new in Rev 5) baseline selection; PL-11 (new in Rev 5) baseline tailoring; RA-01/RA-03 risk assessment; CA-02/CA-07 assessment and monitoring; AT-02 awareness. PL-09/10/11 together provide the governance-select-tailor cycle that mirrors ISMS planning.
clauses.gaps: Minor: COBIT APO13 requires an ISMS approach. SP 800-53 now provides stronger ISMS-compatible controls with PL-09/10/11 for central management, baseline selection, and tailoring. The remaining gap is that SP 800-53 provides controls for security management but isn't itself an ISMS standard (that's NIST RMF).

clauses.title: Managed Data
clauses.rationale: AC-04 data flow; MP family media protection; SC-28 data at rest; SI-12 data management; RA-02 data categorization; PT family privacy; CM-12 (new in Rev 5) information location identifies where sensitive data resides; CM-13 (new in Rev 5) data action mapping documents data processing flows; SI-18 (new in Rev 5) PII quality operations addresses data quality for personal information. These three new controls meaningfully improve data management coverage.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 addresses data security and privacy. CM-12/CM-13/SI-18 close gaps in data location, data flow mapping, and PII quality. COBIT APO14 covers full data management (governance, quality, lifecycle, architecture, metadata). SP 800-53 still doesn't cover master data management, data architecture design, or enterprise data governance beyond security/privacy.

clauses.title: Managed Programs and Projects
clauses.rationale: SA-03 system development lifecycle; PM-07 enterprise architecture; PM-11 mission processes.
clauses.gaps: Major gap. COBIT BAI01 covers IT program and project management methodology. SP 800-53 addresses security in development but not program/project management discipline.

clauses.title: Managed Requirements Definition
clauses.rationale: SA-04 security requirements; SA-08 security engineering; PL-02 security plan; PL-07 concept of operations; PL-08 security architecture.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 covers security requirements definition well. COBIT BAI02 covers all IT requirements (functional, technical, security). Security requirements are a subset.

clauses.title: Managed Solutions Identification and Build
clauses.rationale: SA family covers security in solution development; SA-03 SDLC; SA-10 configuration management; SA-11 testing; SA-20 (new in Rev 5) customized development of critical components addresses bespoke development for high-assurance needs; SA-21 (new in Rev 5) developer screening adds personnel vetting for development teams.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 is strong on security in development. SA-20/SA-21 add critical component development and developer vetting. COBIT BAI03 covers full solution design, build, and quality assurance beyond security aspects including solution architecture and data conversion.

clauses.title: Managed Availability and Capacity
clauses.rationale: CP family continuity and recovery; SC-05 availability protection (denial of service); AU-04 audit storage capacity; SI-13 (new in Rev 5) predictive maintenance enables proactive failure prevention through monitoring component reliability and predicting failures.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 addresses availability through continuity and protection. SI-13 predictive maintenance adds proactive capacity/availability management. COBIT BAI04 covers proactive capacity planning, performance monitoring, and resource optimization for all IT services — broader than security availability.

clauses.title: Managed Organizational Change
clauses.rationale: CM-03/CM-04 configuration change control; PM-01 program updates.
clauses.gaps: Major gap. COBIT BAI05 covers organizational change management (people, process, culture change). SP 800-53 CM controls address technical configuration changes, not organizational change management methodology (stakeholder readiness, training plans, resistance management).

clauses.title: Managed IT Changes
clauses.rationale: CM-03 configuration change control; CM-04 impact analysis; CM-05 access restrictions for change; CM-09 configuration management plan; CM-14 (new in Rev 5) signed components verifies integrity of software/firmware changes through cryptographic signatures; SA-10 developer change management.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 CM family is strong on IT change management from a security perspective. CM-14 adds change integrity verification. COBIT BAI06 includes change scheduling, prioritization, release coordination, and emergency change procedures beyond security scope.

clauses.title: Managed IT Change Acceptance and Transitioning
clauses.rationale: CM-03/CM-04 change control and analysis; SA-11 testing; CA-02 assessment.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 covers security testing and acceptance. COBIT BAI07 covers full change acceptance testing, implementation planning, early production support, and post-implementation review.

clauses.title: Managed Knowledge
clauses.rationale: AT family training and awareness; AT-06 (new in Rev 5) training feedback measures training effectiveness and captures lessons learned; PM-13 workforce development; SA-05 system documentation.
clauses.gaps: AT-06 improves knowledge feedback loops. Major gap remains: COBIT BAI08 covers enterprise knowledge management including knowledge repositories, tacit knowledge capture, and knowledge sharing platforms. SP 800-53 addresses security training and documentation but not systematic knowledge management.

clauses.title: Managed Assets
clauses.rationale: CM-08 component inventory; CM-12 (new in Rev 5) information location tracks where information resides, strengthening asset-data linkage; PM-05 system inventory; MP family media assets; SA-22 unsupported components.
clauses.gaps: CM-12 improves asset-to-data mapping. SP 800-53 covers IT asset inventory and media management. COBIT BAI09 covers full IT asset lifecycle management including financial tracking, license management, and asset optimization.

clauses.title: Managed Configuration
clauses.rationale: CM family comprehensive for configuration management: baselines (CM-02), change control (CM-03), settings (CM-06), inventory (CM-08), plan (CM-09); CM-12 (new in Rev 5) information location ties data to configuration items; CM-13 (new in Rev 5) data action mapping documents processing flows across configured components; CM-14 (new in Rev 5) signed components ensures configuration integrity through cryptographic verification.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 CM family now aligns very well with COBIT BAI10. CM-12, CM-13, and CM-14 close previous gaps. Minor remaining gap: COBIT includes CMDB/configuration repository management and broader IT service configuration item relationships.

clauses.title: Managed IT Projects
clauses.rationale: SA-03 system development lifecycle provides project integration; PM-07 enterprise architecture aligns projects to architecture; PM-10 authorization process gates project delivery; PM-11 mission alignment ensures projects support business processes; CA-05 plan of action and milestones tracks project security deliverables.
clauses.gaps: Major gap. COBIT BAI11 covers IT project management methodology, project governance, stakeholder management, project scope/schedule/resource management, and quality/risk management within projects. SP 800-53 doesn't have project management controls; it addresses security within projects but not project management discipline itself (scheduling, resource allocation, milestone tracking, earned value management).

clauses.title: Managed Operations
clauses.rationale: PE family physical/environmental including PE-21 (new in Rev 5) electromagnetic pulse protection, PE-22 (new in Rev 5) component marking for physical identification, PE-23 (new in Rev 5) facility location for physical security siting; MA family maintenance including MA-07 (new in Rev 5) field maintenance for off-site equipment servicing; SI-04 monitoring; CA-07 continuous monitoring. New PE and MA controls expand facilities and maintenance coverage.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 covers security operations including expanded physical and maintenance controls. COBIT DSS01 covers all IT operations (job scheduling, output management, facilities management, capacity monitoring, environmental management) beyond security scope. PE-21/22/23 and MA-07 add depth but don't address operational management disciplines.

clauses.title: Managed Service Requests and Incidents
clauses.rationale: IR family is comprehensive for security incident management; IR-09 (new in Rev 5) information spillage response adds specific handling for data breach/spillage incidents which is increasingly important.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 covers security incidents comprehensively. IR-09 adds spillage-specific response. COBIT DSS02 covers all IT service requests and incidents (not just security). Service desk, request fulfillment, and non-security incident management remain gaps.

clauses.title: Managed Problems
clauses.rationale: IR-04/IR-05 incident handling/monitoring; SI-02 flaw remediation; CA-05 POA&M.
clauses.gaps: Major gap. COBIT DSS03 covers ITIL-style problem management (root cause analysis, known error database, proactive problem identification). SP 800-53 addresses incident response and flaw remediation but not formal problem management methodology.

clauses.title: Managed Continuity
clauses.rationale: CP family comprehensively covers IT contingency planning, BIA, testing, recovery, alternate sites and processing.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 CP family aligns well. Minor gap: COBIT DSS04 includes business continuity (not just IT), crisis communication, and post-resumption review beyond IT contingency scope.

clauses.title: Managed Security Services
clauses.rationale: SP 800-53 comprehensively covers security services: network protection (SC-07), malware protection (SI-03), monitoring (SI-04), access control (AC family), identity (IA family), physical (PE family). New Rev 5 additions: SC-24 fail in known state for resilient security services; SC-44 detonation chambers (sandboxing) for malware analysis; SC-41 port and I/O device access; SI-16 memory protection (DEP/ASLR); CM-14 signed components for software integrity.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 is very strong here. SC-24/SC-44/SI-16/CM-14 add depth to security service capabilities. Minor gap: COBIT DSS05 frames security as a service management function with specific security service definitions and service-level expectations.

clauses.title: Managed Business Process Controls
clauses.rationale: AC family access controls; AU family audit; SI-10 (information input validation) adds application-level input verification that supports business process control integrity; SI-15 (information output filtering) provides output controls for data leaving systems.
clauses.gaps: SI-10/SI-15 add input validation and output filtering that partially address business process controls. COBIT DSS06 covers business process controls including transaction processing integrity, input/output controls, and business process assurance. SP 800-53 addresses system-level controls but not business process design, segregation of business duties, or transaction-level reconciliation.

clauses.title: Managed Performance and Conformance Monitoring
clauses.rationale: CA-07 continuous monitoring; PM-06 measures of performance; AU-06 audit review; SI-04 system monitoring.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 covers security performance monitoring. COBIT MEA01 covers all IT performance and conformance monitoring including non-security KPIs, service level achievement, and process performance.

clauses.title: Managed System of Internal Control
clauses.rationale: CA-02 security assessments; CA-07 continuous monitoring; PM-06 performance measures; AU-06 audit review.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 covers security control assessment. COBIT MEA02 covers the full internal control system for IT (SOX compliance, control self-assessment, gap remediation). Broader than security controls.

clauses.title: Managed Compliance with External Requirements
clauses.rationale: CA-02 compliance assessment; PM-01 program compliance; PL-04 rules of behavior; SA-04 contractual requirements.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 addresses security compliance. COBIT MEA03 covers all external IT compliance (regulatory, contractual, standards) including compliance program management and impact assessment.

clauses.title: Managed Assurance
clauses.rationale: CA-01 assessment policy; CA-02 security assessments; CA-07 continuous monitoring; CA-08 penetration testing; CA-09 (new in Rev 5) internal system connections authorizes and monitors internal connections, supporting assurance of interconnection integrity.
clauses.gaps: CA-09 adds internal connection assurance. SP 800-53 provides security assurance capabilities. COBIT MEA04 covers enterprise-wide IT assurance planning, independent assurance reviews, and assurance reporting for all IT objectives — broader than security assurance.

frameworks.name: CIS Controls v8
frameworks.description: Prioritized set of actions to protect organizations and data from known cyber attack vectors. Developed by a global community of IT experts.

metadata.disclaimer: Based on publicly available crosswalks and expert analysis. Incorporates all 303 active SP 800-53 Rev 5 controls including new Rev 5 additions (CM-12, CM-13, CM-14, AT-06, SC-44, SC-45, SI-16, SC-47, SC-48, IR-09). Validate with qualified assessors for compliance/audit use.

clauses.title: Inventory and Control of Enterprise Assets
clauses.rationale: CM-08 directly covers component inventory with automated discovery and tracking enhancements. CM-12 (new in Rev 5) addresses information location, strengthening asset-to-data mapping. PM-05 system inventory. Comprehensive asset management.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. CIS 1 includes active/passive asset discovery techniques; CM-08 enhancements and CM-12 information location cover the intent.

clauses.title: Establish and Maintain Detailed Enterprise Asset Inventory
clauses.rationale: CM-08 directly requires system component inventory with detail. CM-12 (new in Rev 5) adds information location tracking which strengthens asset-data linkage.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. CIS emphasizes encrypted and authenticated network management; SP 800-53 covers through remote access, change management, and transmission protection controls.

clauses.title: Establish and Maintain Architecture Diagram(s)
clauses.rationale: PL-02 system security plans (include system architecture); PL-08 security architecture documentation. Architecture documentation partially covered.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CIS specifically requires network architecture diagrams. PL-02/PL-08 require architecture documentation as part of security plans but dedicated diagram requirements are less explicit.

clauses.title: Centralize Network Authentication, Authorization, and Auditing (AAA)
clauses.rationale: AC-02(01) automated account management; IA-02 identification and authentication; AU-06(04) central audit review. Centralized AAA partially covered.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CIS specifically requires centralized AAA (RADIUS/TACACS+). SP 800-53 supports centralized authentication and auditing but specific AAA server requirements are implementation details.

clauses.title: Use of Secure Network Management and Communication Protocols
clauses.rationale: SC-08 transmission confidentiality/integrity; SC-08(01) cryptographic protection; AC-17 remote access. Secure management protocols covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. CIS specifies SSH, HTTPS, TLS for management; SC-08 covers encrypted communications generally.

clauses.title: Ensure Remote Devices Utilize a VPN and are Connecting to an Enterprise's AAA Infrastructure
clauses.rationale: AC-17 remote access; AC-17(02) protection of confidentiality/integrity using encryption; IA-02 identification and authentication. VPN and enterprise authentication covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Establish and Maintain Dedicated Computing Resources for All Administrative Work
clauses.rationale: AC-06(05) privileged accounts; SC-07 boundary protection; SC-32 system partitioning. Dedicated admin workstations/jump servers partially covered.
clauses.gaps: CIS specifically requires privileged access workstations (PAWs) or jump servers. SP 800-53 covers privileged account separation and partitioning but dedicated admin computing resources are an implementation detail.

clauses.title: Network Monitoring and Defense
clauses.rationale: SI-04 system monitoring; AU-06 audit review; SC-07 boundary protection; IR-04 incident handling; CA-07 continuous monitoring; SC-48 (new in Rev 5) sensor relocation for advanced monitoring.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. SP 800-53 monitoring and defense controls are comprehensive. SC-48 adds sensor relocation capability.

clauses.title: Centralize Security Event Alerting
clauses.rationale: SI-04(05) system-generated alerts; AU-06(04) central review and analysis. Centralized alerting well covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Deploy a Host-Based Intrusion Detection Solution
clauses.rationale: SI-04 system monitoring including host-level; SI-07 software, firmware, and information integrity. Host-based IDS covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. CIS specifically requires host-based IDS (HIDS); SI-04 covers system monitoring at all levels including host-based.

clauses.title: Deploy a Network Intrusion Detection Solution
clauses.rationale: SI-04 system monitoring includes NIDS capability; SC-07 boundary protection with monitoring. Network-based IDS well covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Perform Traffic Filtering Between Network Segments
clauses.rationale: AC-04 information flow enforcement; SC-07 boundary protection; SC-07(05) deny by default. Inter-segment traffic filtering directly covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Manage Access Control for Remote Assets
clauses.rationale: AC-17 remote access; AC-17(01) monitoring and control; AC-20 use of external systems. Remote asset access control covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Collect Network Traffic Flow Logs
clauses.rationale: AU-03 audit record content; SI-04(04) inbound/outbound communications traffic analysis. Network flow data collection covered.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CIS specifically addresses network flow data (NetFlow/IPFIX). SP 800-53 covers through general traffic monitoring.

clauses.title: Deploy a Host-Based Intrusion Prevention Solution
clauses.rationale: SI-04 system monitoring; SI-07 software/firmware integrity; SI-16 memory protection. Host-based prevention covered through monitoring and protection controls.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. CIS specifically requires HIPS; SI-04 monitoring with SI-16 memory protection and SI-07 integrity provide equivalent capability.

clauses.title: Deploy a Network Intrusion Prevention Solution
clauses.rationale: SC-07 boundary protection with active traffic filtering; SI-04(04) inbound/outbound traffic analysis. NIPS capability covered.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CIS specifically addresses inline network prevention. SP 800-53 covers through boundary protection and monitoring controls.

clauses.title: Deploy Port-Level Access Control
clauses.rationale: AC-03 access enforcement; SC-07 boundary protection; IA-03 device identification and authentication (802.1X). Port-level access control well covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. CIS references 802.1X; IA-03 device authentication covers this.

clauses.title: Perform Application Layer Filtering
clauses.rationale: SC-07 boundary protection; AC-04 information flow enforcement; SI-04(04) inbound/outbound analysis. Application-layer filtering partially covered.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CIS specifically requires application-layer (L7) filtering/inspection. SP 800-53 covers through boundary protection and information flow but specific L7 inspection is an implementation detail.

clauses.title: Tune Security Event Alerting Thresholds
clauses.rationale: SI-04(05) system-generated alerts; SI-04(07) automated response to suspicious events; AU-06 audit review analysis. Alert tuning partially covered.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CIS specifically requires tuning of alert thresholds to reduce false positives/negatives. SP 800-53 requires alerting and analysis but threshold tuning optimization is an implementation detail.

clauses.title: Security Awareness and Skills Training
clauses.rationale: AT family comprehensive: AT-01 policy; AT-02 awareness; AT-03 role-based training; AT-04 records; AT-06 (new in Rev 5) training feedback; PM-13 workforce; PM-14 testing. AT-06 strengthens training effectiveness measurement.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. AT-06 training feedback adds measurability to training program.

clauses.title: Establish and Maintain a Security Awareness Program
clauses.rationale: AT-01 awareness and training policy; AT-02 security awareness training; PM-13 information security workforce. Program establishment directly covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Train Workforce Members to Recognize Social Engineering Attacks
clauses.rationale: AT-02(02) practical exercises including social engineering awareness. SP 800-53 Rev 5 explicitly includes social engineering training.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Train Workforce Members on Authentication Best Practices
clauses.rationale: AT-02 security awareness training; AT-03 role-based training; IA-05 authenticator management (includes user training on password practices). Authentication training covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. CIS specifically addresses authentication best practices training; AT-02/AT-03 cover through general security awareness.

clauses.title: Train Workforce on Data Handling Best Practices
clauses.rationale: AT-02/AT-03 training includes data handling; MP-01 media protection policy establishes handling requirements for training.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CIS is specific about data handling training topics. SP 800-53 includes through general training programs.

clauses.title: Train Workforce Members on Causes of Unintentional Data Exposure
clauses.rationale: AT-02 security awareness (includes data exposure risks); AT-03 role-based training; MP-01 media protection policy and awareness.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CIS is specific about unintentional data exposure training. SP 800-53 covers through general awareness and media protection training.

clauses.title: Train Workforce Members on Recognizing and Reporting Security Incidents
clauses.rationale: AT-02 security awareness including incident recognition; IR-02 incident response training; AT-06 (new in Rev 5) training feedback on training effectiveness. Incident recognition and reporting training well covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Train Workforce on How to Identify and Report if Their Enterprise Assets are Missing Security Updates
clauses.rationale: AT-02 security awareness; AT-03 role-based training; SI-02 flaw remediation. Security update awareness partially covered.
clauses.gaps: CIS specifically addresses training on identifying missing security updates. SP 800-53 covers general security awareness and flaw remediation but this specific training topic is an implementation detail.

clauses.title: Train Workforce on the Dangers of Connecting to and Transmitting Enterprise Data Over Insecure Networks
clauses.rationale: AT-02 security awareness; AT-03 role-based training; AC-17 remote access policy. Insecure network awareness partially covered.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CIS specifically addresses insecure network dangers training. SP 800-53 covers through general awareness and remote access policies.

clauses.title: Conduct Role-Specific Security Awareness and Skills Training
clauses.rationale: AT-03 role-based security training; AT-06 (new in Rev 5) training feedback for measuring effectiveness; PM-13 information security workforce development. Role-specific training directly covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. AT-06 training feedback adds measurement capability to role-based training programs.

clauses.title: Service Provider Management
clauses.rationale: SA-04 acquisition process; SA-09 external system services; SR family supply chain risk management. Comprehensive service provider security management.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CIS 15 includes specific guidance on classifying service providers and monitoring. SP 800-53 covers through acquisition and supply chain controls.

clauses.title: Establish and Maintain an Inventory of Service Providers
clauses.rationale: SA-09 external information system services require identification of providers; PM-05 system inventory can include service providers.
clauses.gaps: CIS specifically requires a dedicated service provider inventory. SP 800-53 implies but does not explicitly mandate a service provider register.

clauses.title: Establish and Maintain a Service Provider Management Policy
clauses.rationale: SA-04 acquisition security requirements; SA-09 external system services policy; SR-01 supply chain risk management policy.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. Service provider management policy covered through acquisition and supply chain controls.

clauses.title: Classify Service Providers
clauses.rationale: RA-02 security categorization; SA-09 external services assessment; SR-02 supply chain risk management plan. Classification partially covered.
clauses.gaps: CIS specifically requires classifying service providers by data sensitivity and criticality. SP 800-53 categorizes systems/data but service provider classification as a distinct activity is less explicit.

clauses.title: Ensure Service Provider Contracts Include Security Requirements
clauses.rationale: SA-04 acquisition process including security requirements in contracts; SA-09 external service agreements; SR-03 supply chain controls and processes.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Assess Service Providers
clauses.rationale: SR-06 supplier assessments and reviews; SA-09 external service monitoring; CA-02 control assessments. Service provider assessment covered.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CIS requires periodic assessment of service providers. SR-06 and CA-02 cover assessments but specific service provider audit cadence is an organizational decision.

clauses.title: Monitor Service Providers
clauses.rationale: SA-09 external service monitoring; SR-06 supplier assessments; CA-07 continuous monitoring. Ongoing monitoring partially covered.
clauses.gaps: CIS requires continuous monitoring of service provider security posture. SP 800-53 covers monitoring but dedicated service provider monitoring cadence is less explicit.

clauses.title: Securely Decommission Service Providers
clauses.rationale: SA-09 external services; PS-04 personnel termination (access revocation concept); MP-06 media sanitization. Decommissioning partially covered.
clauses.gaps: CIS specifically addresses service provider decommissioning including data return/destruction. SP 800-53 covers through general service and media controls but specific provider offboarding procedures are not a dedicated control.

clauses.title: Application Software Security
clauses.rationale: SA family comprehensive for application security: SDLC (SA-03), requirements (SA-04), engineering (SA-08), configuration management (SA-10), testing (SA-11), standards (SA-15), architecture (SA-17).
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Establish and Maintain a Secure Application Development Process
clauses.rationale: SA-03 system development life cycle; SA-15 development process, standards, and tools. Secure SDLC directly covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Establish and Maintain a Process to Accept and Address Software Vulnerabilities
clauses.rationale: SI-02 flaw remediation; RA-05 vulnerability management; SA-11 developer security testing. Vulnerability acceptance and remediation process covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Perform Root Cause Analysis on Security Vulnerabilities
clauses.rationale: SA-11 developer security testing (includes analysis); IR-03 incident response testing/lessons learned; CA-05 POA&M tracking. Root cause analysis partially covered.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CIS specifically requires root cause analysis for vulnerabilities. SP 800-53 covers through testing, lessons learned, and remediation tracking but dedicated root cause analysis is not a single control.

clauses.title: Establish and Manage an Inventory of Third-Party Software Components
clauses.rationale: CM-08 system component inventory; SA-10 developer configuration management; SR-04 provenance (component origin tracking). Third-party component inventory partially covered.
clauses.gaps: CIS specifically requires software bill of materials (SBOM) or third-party component inventory. SP 800-53 covers through component inventory and provenance controls but dedicated SBOM requirements are less explicit.

clauses.title: Use Up-to-Date and Trusted Third-Party Software Components
clauses.rationale: SA-22 unsupported components; SR-04 provenance; SR-11 component authenticity. Third-party component currency and trust partially covered.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CIS specifically requires using current, trusted third-party components. SP 800-53 covers through support, provenance, and authenticity controls.

clauses.title: Establish and Maintain a Severity Rating System and Process for Application Vulnerabilities
clauses.rationale: RA-05 vulnerability scanning includes severity ratings; RA-03 risk assessment includes risk ranking. Severity rating concept covered.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CIS specifically requires a severity rating system for application vulnerabilities. RA-05 and RA-03 cover risk/vulnerability ranking but a dedicated severity system is an implementation detail.

clauses.title: Use Standard Hardening Configuration Templates for Application Infrastructure
clauses.rationale: CM-02 baseline configuration; CM-06 configuration settings; CM-03 change control. Hardened image concept covered through baselines.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CIS specifically addresses golden/hardened images for application infrastructure. SP 800-53 uses baseline concept which is similar.

clauses.title: Separate Production and Non-Production Systems
clauses.rationale: CM-04 impact analysis (separate test environments); SA-11 developer testing environment; SC-32 system partitioning. Environment separation addressed.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CIS specifically requires production/non-production separation. SP 800-53 implies through testing and partitioning controls.

clauses.title: Train Developers in Application Security Concepts and Secure Coding
clauses.rationale: AT-03 role-based security training (developers); SA-16 developer-provided training. Secure coding training covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Apply Secure Design Principles in Application Architectures
clauses.rationale: SA-08 security and privacy engineering principles; SA-17 developer security and privacy architecture. Secure design principles directly and comprehensively covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Leverage Vetted Modules or Services for Application Security Components
clauses.rationale: SA-08 security engineering principles; SC-13 cryptographic protection (use vetted cryptographic modules); SR-04 provenance. Vetted components partially covered.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CIS specifically requires using vetted security modules (e.g., FIPS-validated crypto). SC-13 covers cryptographic modules; broader vetted security component usage is less explicitly mandated.

clauses.title: Implement Code-Level Security Checks
clauses.rationale: SA-11(01) static code analysis; SA-11(02) dynamic code analysis. Code-level security checks directly covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Conduct Application Penetration Testing
clauses.rationale: CA-08 penetration testing; SA-11(05) penetration testing enhancement. Application penetration testing well covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Conduct Threat Modeling
clauses.rationale: SA-08 security engineering principles; SA-17 developer security architecture; RA-03 risk assessment. Threat modeling partially covered.
clauses.gaps: CIS specifically requires threat modeling as a distinct activity. SP 800-53 covers threat analysis through risk assessment and security engineering but threat modeling as a formal methodology (STRIDE, PASTA) is not a dedicated control.

clauses.title: Incident Response Management
clauses.rationale: IR family comprehensively covers incident response management. IR-09 information spillage response adds data breach-specific handling.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Designate Personnel to Manage Incident Handling
clauses.rationale: IR-01/IR-02 incident response roles and training; PM-02 security role assignment including incident response personnel.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Establish and Maintain Contact Information for Reporting Security Incidents
clauses.rationale: IR-06 incident reporting contacts; IR-07 incident response assistance (external contacts); PM-15 contacts with security groups. Contact information for incident reporting covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Establish and Maintain an Enterprise Process for Reporting Incidents
clauses.rationale: IR-06 incident reporting procedures; IR-08 incident response plan with reporting processes. Enterprise reporting process directly covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Establish and Maintain an Incident Response Process
clauses.rationale: IR-08 incident response plan; IR-01 incident response policy and procedures. Direct and comprehensive mapping.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Assign Key Roles and Responsibilities
clauses.rationale: IR-01 incident response policy (roles); IR-02 incident response training (role-based); PM-02 security role assignment. Key roles and responsibilities directly covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Define Mechanisms for Communicating During Incident Response
clauses.rationale: IR-04 incident handling including communications; IR-06 incident reporting; IR-07 incident response assistance; SC-47 (new in Rev 5) alternate communications paths. Communication mechanisms well covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. SC-47 alternate communications paths strengthens incident communication resilience.

clauses.title: Conduct Routine Incident Response Exercises
clauses.rationale: IR-03 incident response testing with exercises; PM-14 testing, training, and monitoring. Incident response exercises directly covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Conduct Post-Incident Reviews
clauses.rationale: IR-03 incident response testing/lessons learned; IR-04 incident handling includes post-incident analysis and lessons learned activities.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Establish and Maintain Security Incident Thresholds
clauses.rationale: IR-04 incident handling with escalation criteria; IR-05 incident monitoring with thresholds; IR-08 incident response plan including severity levels.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CIS specifically requires defined incident thresholds and escalation criteria. SP 800-53 covers through incident handling and monitoring but formal threshold definition is an implementation detail.

clauses.title: Penetration Testing
clauses.rationale: CA-08 penetration testing; CA-08(01) independent penetration testing agent; RA-05 vulnerability assessment. Comprehensive penetration testing coverage.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Establish and Maintain a Penetration Testing Program
clauses.rationale: CA-08 directly establishes penetration testing requirements and program.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Perform Periodic External Penetration Tests
clauses.rationale: CA-08 covers penetration testing. External perspective specified through testing scope definition.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CIS specifically addresses external penetration testing cadence and scope. CA-08 covers testing generally; external vs. internal distinction is a scope decision.

clauses.title: Remediate Penetration Test Findings
clauses.rationale: CA-05 plan of action and milestones for remediation tracking; SI-02 flaw remediation. Finding remediation directly covered.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Validate Security Measures
clauses.rationale: CA-02 control assessments (validation); CA-08 penetration testing; RA-05 vulnerability assessment. Security measure validation covered through multiple controls.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Perform Periodic Internal Penetration Tests
clauses.rationale: CA-08 covers penetration testing. Internal perspective specified through testing scope definition.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CIS specifically addresses internal penetration testing cadence and scope. CA-08 covers testing generally; internal vs. external distinction is a scope decision.

frameworks.name: NIST CSF 2.0
frameworks.description: Voluntary guidance for managing and reducing cybersecurity risk. Organized around five core functions: Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover.

metadata.disclaimer: Based on publicly available crosswalks and expert analysis. Validate with qualified assessors for compliance/audit use.

crosswalk_check.source: NIST, CSF 2.0 to SP 800-53 Rev 5.2.0 crosswalk, v1.0.0 (OLIR entry 186, posted 2025-11-17)
crosswalk_check.scope: Base controls only. NIST's crosswalk is the base of this mapping: every pair in it is here, except for withdrawn controls. 503 pairs were added on 2026-10-03, and 5 more the same day with IA-13 and SA-24, when OSA's catalogue gained those two controls. Pairs OSA records that the crosswalk does not are kept and listed under not_in_source. Rows naming a category or a whole control family, not a subcategory and a control, were not used. The crosswalk also pairs RA-04, which SP 800-53 Rev 5 withdrew. The coverage figures, rationales and gaps are OSA's, written for OSA's own pairs, and were not revised. The file fetched from NIST does not carry the checksum NIST's catalogue lists for it; both are given.

clauses.title: The organizational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management
clauses.rationale: PM-07 enterprise architecture; PM-08 critical infrastructure; PM-11 mission/business process definition. Mission context well addressed.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 emphasizes organizational context beyond pure security mission alignment.

clauses.title: Internal and external stakeholders are understood, and their needs and expectations regarding cybersecurity risk management are understood and considered
clauses.rationale: PM-08 critical infrastructure planning includes stakeholders; PM-11 mission process definition; PM-15 security contacts.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 requires systematic stakeholder identification and expectation analysis. SP 800-53 partially addresses through program-level controls.

clauses.title: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity are understood and managed
clauses.rationale: PM-01 program plan addresses legal context; PL-04 rules of behavior; SA-04 contractual requirements.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 lacks a dedicated legal/regulatory requirements identification control. Federal compliance assumed in FISMA context.

clauses.title: Critical objectives, capabilities, and services that external stakeholders depend on are understood and communicated
clauses.rationale: PM-08 critical infrastructure; PM-11 mission processes; CP-02 contingency planning includes critical service identification.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 requires explicit identification of stakeholder-dependent services. SP 800-53 addresses through mission/business process controls but less explicitly.

clauses.title: Outcomes, capabilities, and services that the organization depends on are understood and communicated
clauses.rationale: PM-08/PM-11 mission/business dependencies; SA-09 external services; CP-02 contingency planning.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 emphasizes understanding dependencies from supply chain and partner services. SP 800-53 partially covers through contingency and supply chain controls.

clauses.title: Risk management objectives are established and expressed as statements that articulate the basis for cybersecurity risk management decisions
clauses.rationale: PM-09 risk management strategy; PM-28 risk framing; RA-01 risk assessment policy.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 emphasizes explicit risk management objectives. SP 800-53 covers through risk strategy and framing.

clauses.title: Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established, communicated, and maintained
clauses.rationale: PM-09 risk management strategy includes risk tolerance; PM-28 risk framing.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 requires explicit risk appetite statements. SP 800-53 addresses risk tolerance within strategy.

clauses.title: Cybersecurity risk management activities and outcomes are included in enterprise risk management processes
clauses.rationale: PM-09 risk management strategy; PM-28 risk framing at enterprise level; PM-01 program integration.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 emphasizes ERM integration. SP 800-53 supports but the integration with non-security enterprise risk is less explicit.

clauses.title: Strategic direction that describes appropriate risk response options is established and communicated
clauses.rationale: PM-09 risk strategy; RA-03 risk response identification; RA-07 risk response (new in Rev 5) directly addresses risk response options including accept, mitigate, share, or avoid; CA-05 remediation planning.
clauses.gaps: Minor: RA-07 significantly closes the gap by mandating risk response in accordance with risk tolerance.

clauses.title: Lines of communication across the organization are established for cybersecurity risks, including risks from suppliers and other third parties
clauses.rationale: PM-15 security contacts; PM-16 threat awareness; IR-06/IR-07 incident communication; SR-01 supply chain risk.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 emphasizes organizational risk communication pathways. SP 800-53 covers specific communication channels but systematic risk communication planning less explicit.

clauses.title: A standardized method for calculating, documenting, categorizing, and prioritizing cybersecurity risks is established and communicated
clauses.rationale: RA-01 risk assessment policy; RA-02 categorization; RA-03 risk assessment methodology; PM-09 risk strategy.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 requires standardized risk calculation methodology. SP 800-53 RA-03 covers comprehensive risk assessment.

clauses.title: Strategic opportunities (positive risks) are characterized and are included in organizational cybersecurity risk discussions
clauses.rationale: PM-09 risk management strategy may include opportunity considerations.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 explicitly addresses positive risks/opportunities. SP 800-53 is threat/vulnerability focused and does not address strategic opportunities.

clauses.title: Organizational leadership is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk and fosters a culture that is risk-aware, ethical, and continually improving
clauses.rationale: PM-01 program plan; PM-02 senior security role; PM-13 workforce; AT-02 awareness.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 emphasizes leadership accountability and culture. SP 800-53 addresses roles and awareness but organizational culture is less explicit.

clauses.title: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, understood, and enforced
clauses.rationale: PM-02 role assignment; PS-01/PS-02 personnel roles; PS-09 position descriptions (new in Rev 5) explicitly incorporates security roles into position descriptions; PL-01 planning roles; PM-13 workforce.
clauses.gaps: Minimal: PS-09 strengthens the mapping by requiring security roles in position descriptions.

clauses.title: Adequate resources are allocated commensurate with the cybersecurity risk strategy, roles and responsibilities, and policies
clauses.rationale: PM-03 information security resources; PM-13 workforce resources; SA-02 allocation of resources.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 ties resource allocation to risk strategy. PM-03 addresses resources but risk-proportional allocation less explicit.

clauses.title: Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices
clauses.rationale: PS family comprehensive for personnel security; PS-09 position descriptions (new in Rev 5); AT family for training; PM-13 workforce development.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. SP 800-53 PS/AT families well aligned with HR security practices.

clauses.title: A policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established based on organizational context, cybersecurity strategy, and priorities and is communicated and enforced
clauses.rationale: PL-01 planning policy and procedures; PM-01 information security program plan; PM-09 risk management strategy; PL-02 system security plans. Every control family has an -01 policy control.
clauses.gaps: Minimal: SP 800-53 requires policy for each family and a comprehensive program plan. Well aligned with CSF policy requirements.

clauses.title: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is reviewed, updated, communicated, and enforced to reflect changes in requirements, threats, technology, and organizational mission
clauses.rationale: PL-01 includes periodic review; PM-01 program plan updates; PM-04 plan of action and milestones tracks needed changes; CA-07 continuous monitoring informs policy updates.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 emphasizes policy review driven by threat landscape changes. SP 800-53 family -01 controls require periodic review but threat-driven updates are less explicit.

clauses.title: Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed to inform and adjust strategy and direction
clauses.rationale: PM-09 risk management strategy review; PM-06 measures of performance; CA-07 continuous monitoring; PM-31 continuous monitoring strategy.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 emphasizes strategic-level outcome review. SP 800-53 covers through monitoring and performance measures but explicit strategic adjustment is less formalized.

clauses.title: The cybersecurity risk management strategy is reviewed and adjusted to ensure coverage of organizational requirements and risks
clauses.rationale: PM-09 risk strategy; PM-28 risk framing; CA-02 security assessments inform strategy; RA-03 risk assessment.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 requires systematic strategy review for coverage. SP 800-53 addresses through risk assessment and strategy controls but explicit coverage reviews are less mandated.

clauses.title: Organizational cybersecurity risk management performance is evaluated and reviewed for adjustments needed
clauses.rationale: PM-06 measures of performance; CA-07 continuous monitoring; PM-14 testing, training, and monitoring; CA-02 assessment results.
clauses.gaps: Minor: SP 800-53 provides strong assessment and monitoring capabilities for performance evaluation.

clauses.title: A cybersecurity supply chain risk management program, strategy, objectives, policies, and processes are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders
clauses.rationale: SR-01 supply chain risk management policy; SR-02 supply chain controls; SR-03 supply chain risk assessment; PM-30 supply chain risk management.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. SP 800-53 Rev 5 SR family is well aligned with CSF supply chain governance.

clauses.title: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities for suppliers, customers, and partners are established and communicated
clauses.rationale: SA-04 acquisition requirements; SA-09 external services; SR-01/SR-03 supply chain roles and assessments.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 specifically addresses customer and partner roles. SP 800-53 focuses on supplier roles.

clauses.title: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management is integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management, risk assessment, and improvement processes
clauses.rationale: SR-01/SR-02 supply chain integration; PM-09 risk strategy integration; PM-30 supply chain risk management plan.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 emphasizes integration with broader enterprise risk. SP 800-53 addresses supply chain risk management but enterprise-wide integration is less explicit.

clauses.title: Suppliers are known and prioritized by criticality
clauses.rationale: SR-02 supply chain risk management plan covers supplier identification; SR-03 supply chain risk assessment includes criticality; SR-06 supplier assessments; SA-04 acquisition with security requirements.
clauses.gaps: Minor: SP 800-53 covers supplier criticality assessment through SR-03 risk assessment and SR-06 reviews.

clauses.title: Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are established, prioritized, and integrated into contracts and other types of agreements with suppliers and other relevant third parties
clauses.rationale: SA-04 acquisition processes include security requirements in contracts; SR-01 supply chain policy; SR-02 supply chain plan; SR-03 controls and processes.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. SA-04 directly addresses contract requirements.

clauses.title: Planning and due diligence are conducted to reduce risks before entering into formal supplier or other third-party relationships
clauses.rationale: SR-03 supply chain controls; SR-05 acquisition strategies, tools, and methods; SR-06 supplier assessments and reviews; SA-04 acquisition processes.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 emphasizes pre-engagement due diligence. SP 800-53 covers through acquisition and assessment controls.

clauses.title: The risks posed by a supplier, their products and services, and other third parties are understood, recorded, prioritized, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship
clauses.rationale: SR-02 supply chain plan; SR-03 ongoing supply chain assessment; SR-06 supplier reviews; RA-03 risk assessment; RA-07 risk response (new in Rev 5) ensures risk findings are responded to.
clauses.gaps: Minor: RA-07 strengthens coverage by ensuring systematic risk response. Ongoing monitoring through supplier relationship lifecycle is well covered.

clauses.title: Relevant suppliers and other third parties are included in incident planning, response, and recovery activities
clauses.rationale: IR-04 incident handling coordination; IR-08 incident response plan; SR-08 notification agreements; CP-02 contingency plan.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 emphasizes supplier inclusion in incident response. SR-08 notification agreements address communication but active supplier participation in exercises is less explicit.

clauses.title: Supply chain security practices are integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management programs, and their performance is monitored throughout the technology product and service life cycle
clauses.rationale: SR-01/SR-02/SR-03 supply chain risk management lifecycle; SR-06 ongoing assessments; PM-30 program integration; SA-03 system development lifecycle.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 emphasizes lifecycle monitoring of supply chain practices. SP 800-53 covers through supply chain and lifecycle controls.

clauses.title: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management plans include provisions for activities that occur after the conclusion of a partnership or service agreement
clauses.rationale: SR-12 component disposal; SA-04 acquisition/decommission requirements; SR-01 supply chain policy may cover termination; MP-06 media sanitization.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 specifically addresses post-relationship supply chain activities. SP 800-53 covers disposal but relationship termination planning is less formalized.

clauses.title: Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained
clauses.rationale: CM-08 directly covers hardware component inventory with automated discovery; PM-05 system inventory.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained
clauses.rationale: CM-08 component inventory (includes software); PM-05 system inventory; CM-10 software usage.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Representations of the organization's authorized network communication and internal and external network data flows are maintained
clauses.rationale: AC-04 information flow enforcement; PL-08 security architecture; CA-03 information exchange; SC-07 boundary definition; CM-12 information location (new in Rev 5) documents where information resides and how it flows.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CM-12 strengthens coverage by requiring documentation of information location and processing across system components.

clauses.title: Inventories of services provided by suppliers are maintained
clauses.rationale: SA-09 external services identification; SR-06 supplier assessments; PM-05 system inventory.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 requires specific supplier service inventory. SP 800-53 covers through external service controls but dedicated inventory less explicit.

clauses.title: Assets are prioritized based on classification, criticality, resources, and impact to the mission
clauses.rationale: RA-02 security categorization; PM-11 mission process definition; CP-02 contingency priority; PM-07 architecture priorities.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 combines multiple prioritization criteria. SP 800-53 covers through categorization and mission analysis.

clauses.title: Inventories of data and corresponding metadata for designated data types are maintained
clauses.rationale: RA-02 data categorization; CM-08 component inventory; CM-12 information location (new in Rev 5) identifies and documents data locations; CM-13 data action mapping (new in Rev 5) maps data processing actions; SI-12 information management.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CM-12 and CM-13 significantly improve coverage by addressing data location tracking and data action mapping. Explicit metadata inventory management remains less formalized.

clauses.title: Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycles
clauses.rationale: SA-03 SDLC; SA-22 unsupported components; CM-08 inventory lifecycle; SI-12 data lifecycle; MP-06 media sanitization.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 requires holistic lifecycle management. SP 800-53 covers through various lifecycle controls.

clauses.title: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded
clauses.rationale: RA-05 vulnerability identification and scanning; SI-02 flaw identification; SI-05 vulnerability advisories.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources
clauses.rationale: PM-16 threat awareness program; SI-05 security alerts; PM-15 security contacts.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Internal and external threats to the organization are identified and recorded
clauses.rationale: RA-03 risk assessment includes threat identification; PM-16 threat awareness; RA-10 threat hunting.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Potential impacts and likelihoods of threats exploiting vulnerabilities are identified and recorded
clauses.rationale: RA-03 directly covers impact and likelihood assessment.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response prioritization
clauses.rationale: RA-03 comprehensive risk assessment; RA-07 risk response (new in Rev 5) mandates responding to assessment findings in accordance with risk tolerance; PM-09 risk strategy; CA-05 risk response prioritization.
clauses.gaps: Minimal: RA-07 strengthens coverage by formalizing risk response based on assessment findings.

clauses.title: Risk responses are chosen, prioritized, planned, tracked, and communicated
clauses.rationale: RA-07 risk response (new in Rev 5) is the primary control for risk response actions including accept, mitigate, share, and avoid; RA-03 risk response; PM-09 strategy; CA-05 POA&M tracking; PM-04 plan of action tracking.
clauses.gaps: Minimal: RA-07 directly addresses risk response selection and tracking, significantly improving coverage.

clauses.title: Changes and exceptions are managed, assessed for risk impact, and recorded
clauses.rationale: CM-03 change control; CM-04 impact analysis; CA-06 authorization; RA-07 risk response (new in Rev 5) addresses exception handling through risk acceptance; PM-09 risk management.
clauses.gaps: Minor: RA-07 strengthens exception management through risk tolerance-based response. CSF 2.0 exception management well covered.

clauses.title: Processes for receiving, analyzing, and responding to vulnerability disclosures are established
clauses.rationale: RA-05 vulnerability management; SI-02 remediation; SI-05 advisories; PM-15 information sharing.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 specifically addresses vulnerability disclosure processes (VDP). SP 800-53 covers vulnerability management but formal VDP less explicit.

clauses.title: The authenticity and integrity of hardware and software are assessed prior to acquisition and use
clauses.rationale: SR-04 provenance; SR-05 authenticity; SR-09 tamper resistance; SR-10 inspection; SR-11 component authenticity; SA-04 acquisition requirements.
clauses.gaps: Minor: SP 800-53 SR family covers hardware/software integrity comprehensively.

clauses.title: Critical suppliers are assessed prior to acquisition
clauses.rationale: SR-03 supply chain assessment; SR-05 supply chain controls; SR-06 supplier assessments; SA-04 acquisition requirements.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 emphasizes pre-acquisition supplier assessment. SP 800-53 covers through supply chain and acquisition controls.

clauses.title: Improvements are identified from evaluations
clauses.rationale: CA-02 assessment findings; CA-07 continuous monitoring improvements; PM-06 performance measures; PM-04 POA&M.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 emphasizes systematic improvement identification. SP 800-53 generates findings but improvement process less formalized.

clauses.title: Improvements are identified from security tests and exercises, including those done in coordination with suppliers and relevant third parties
clauses.rationale: CA-08 penetration testing; IR-03 incident response testing; PM-14 testing/exercises; CP-04 contingency testing.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 includes third-party coordination in testing. SP 800-53 covers testing but supplier coordination less explicit.

clauses.title: Improvements are identified from execution of operational processes, procedures, and activities
clauses.rationale: CA-07 continuous monitoring; PM-06 measures; IR-04 incident analysis; SI-04 system monitoring; AT-06 training feedback (new in Rev 5) provides operational feedback on training effectiveness.
clauses.gaps: Minor: AT-06 improves coverage by feeding operational training results back for improvement. CSF 2.0 emphasizes operational improvement identification.

clauses.title: Incident response plans and other cybersecurity plans that affect operations are established, communicated, maintained, and improved based on lessons learned and other factors
clauses.rationale: IR-08 incident response plan; IR-03 testing/lessons learned; CP-02 contingency plan; CP-04 contingency testing.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization
clauses.rationale: IA family comprehensive for identity and credential management.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Identities are proofed and bound to credentials based on the context of interactions
clauses.rationale: IA-12 identity proofing; IA-04 identifier management; IA-05 authenticator management.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Users, services, and hardware are authenticated
clauses.rationale: IA-02 user authentication; IA-03 device authentication; IA-08 non-org users; IA-09 service identification.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Identity assertions are protected, conveyed, and verified
clauses.rationale: IA-02 authentication; IA-05 authenticator management; SC-23 session authenticity; IA-08 non-org users.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 addresses identity federation and assertion protocols. SP 800-53 covers through authentication controls.

clauses.title: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties
clauses.rationale: AC-02 account management; AC-03 access enforcement; AC-05 separation of duties; AC-06 least privilege; AC-24 access control decisions.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Physical access to assets is managed, monitored, and enforced commensurate with risk
clauses.rationale: PE-02 access authorizations; PE-03 access control; PE-06 monitoring; PE-08 access records.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Personnel are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform general tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind
clauses.rationale: AT-02 awareness training; AT-03 role-based training; AT-06 training feedback (new in Rev 5) ensures training effectiveness is measured and reported; PM-13 workforce.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. AT-06 strengthens by providing feedback loop on training results.

clauses.title: Individuals in specialized roles are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform relevant tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind
clauses.rationale: AT-03 role-based training; AT-06 training feedback (new in Rev 5) particularly important for specialized roles where failures indicate serious problems; PM-13 workforce development; IR-02 incident response training.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. AT-06 specifically notes that failures in critical roles may indicate serious problems.

clauses.title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest is protected
clauses.rationale: SC-28 protection at rest; MP-04 media storage; MP-05 media transport; AC-03 access enforcement.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit is protected
clauses.rationale: SC-08 transmission protection; SC-12 key management; SC-13 cryptographic protection; AC-17 remote access.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-use is protected
clauses.rationale: SC-04 information in shared resources; AC-03/AC-04 access and flow control; SC-39 process isolation.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 explicitly addresses data-in-use protection (confidential computing, memory protection). SP 800-53 covers through general controls but data-in-use is less explicitly addressed.

clauses.title: Backups of data are created, protected, maintained, and tested in accordance with policy
clauses.rationale: CP-09 system backup; CP-06 alternate storage.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Configuration management practices are established and applied
clauses.rationale: CM family comprehensive for configuration management; PL-09 central management (new in Rev 5) enables centralized management of configuration controls.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. PL-09 strengthens by enabling centralized configuration management.

clauses.title: Software is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk
